frontier.note: SCHEMA HALF of the Security Passport first-run journey. Adds ONE private table (public.sp_passport_operations), THREE SECURITY DEFINER functions, ONE partial unique index on sp_passport_events, and ONE column on sp_passport_profiles (onboarding_draft_revision). It also TIGHTENS one existing policy -- sp_events_self_insert now refuses a client-written event whose detail carries operation_id or first_merit. No row is rewritten or back-filled and no other existing object changes. THE DEFECT: finishing the first-run wizard performed four independent writes from the browser -- insert the employment period, update the profile, insert two events -- with nothing holding them together, so a failure at any seam left a merit with onboarding still in progress (and the next attempt SKIPPED the insert because a period now existed, leaving the holder unable ever to finish), or a completed profile whose audit events were lost silently because the insert's error was never read. Completion was also not idempotent, and the truthfulness declaration was never checked at all: declared_accurate_at was written unconditionally whenever completion was called, while the tick-box lived only in React state. THE SECOND DEFECT, found by independent review of the first draft of this migration: idempotency was keyed on sp_passport_events.detail->>'operation_id', and that table is directly insertable by authenticated with RLS checking only the holder and actor -- so a signed-in holder could pre-seed an experience_created event carrying any operation id and the function would answer a replay without proving the subject existed, belonged to them, matched the submitted facts, or that onboarding and the declaration had happened. Idempotency now rests on sp_passport_operations, which has NO grant of any kind for anon or authenticated (TRUNCATE included, which RLS does not cover) and RLS enabled and FORCED with no policies, so the Data API cannot reach it; the operation is bound to auth.uid() and to a sha256 fingerprint of exactly the facts submitted, a replay carrying different facts is refused (SP_OPERATION_FACTS_CHANGED), one holder replaying another's id is refused (SP_OPERATION_ID_CONFLICT), and a replay is answered only after re-checking that the recorded subject still exists and still belongs to the caller (SP_OPERATION_SUBJECT_MISSING). sp_passport_ensure commits the profile, its receipt and its creation event in one transaction and repairs a legacy profile that has no receipt. The function is NOT a general merit API: a NEW first-merit operation is refused once the holder holds a current merit (SP_FIRST_MERIT_ALREADY_EXISTS), while the original operation still replays -- and that decision is SERIALISED PER HOLDER with a transaction-scoped advisory lock keyed to auth.uid(), taken before the receipt is claimed, because two DIFFERENT operation ids do not conflict on the receipt's primary key and would otherwise each see no committed merit and each create one. The lock is released at commit or rollback, so it is not a permanent constraint: a holder whose only merit is later archived returns to the first run. Proved with two psql processes carrying different ids (the second waited 3s and was refused; one merit, one receipt, one event set), and a permanent negative control in db-test.sh strips the lock out of the live definition, watches two merits appear, and re-applies this migration. The declaration is stamped with the time it was MADE rather than coalesced onto a legacy timestamp, and a replay preserves it. It names no trust column at all, so the merit takes the self_declared / active column defaults; the migration's postflight and the database suite both assert that, along with the grants, the RLS state and the absence of any policy on the receipts table. DEPLOY ORDER: SCHEMA FIRST and safe alone -- nothing existing calls the functions, the receipts table starts empty, the index is partial on a key no existing row carries, and the column is additive with a default. The tightened events policy breaks no existing client: every application event insert writes a detail object carrying neither key. The dependent application release is held out of merge by schema-first-release-check.ts until this is recorded applied here. Rolling back drops the three functions, the table, the index and the column, and restores the previous events policy; it touches no holder merit, event or profile row, and the db-test.sh rollback proof asserts exactly that before re-applying over the same data. Applied hosted on 2026-09-07 through the connected Lovable/Supabase migration mechanism; see evidenceSource and the release reconciliation record.

frontier.note: SECURITY, FUNCTION-ONLY. Rewrites public.sp_verifier_decide(uuid,text,text,text,text,date,date) and nothing else -- no table, column, constraint, index, policy, trigger or grant change, no row rewritten. Byte-for-byte the 20261013090000 body except one NEW block that binds the verification METHOD to the request kind on an APPROVAL: cqrityjob_review requires document_review (SP_CQRITYJOB_REVIEW_REQUIRES_DOCUMENT_REVIEW), employer_attestation requires employer_confirmation (SP_EMPLOYER_ATTESTATION_REQUIRES_EMPLOYER_CONFIRMATION), and issuer_confirmation is refused for every kind (SP_ISSUER_CONFIRMATION_NOT_AVAILABLE) until a later release introduces a structurally identified issuer organisation, issuer membership and authority, an issuer request kind, a source receipt, revocation authority and their RLS/audit tests. THE DEFECT: a CQrityjob reviewer answering a cqrityjob_review request could record issuer_confirmation or employer_confirmation, and every surface then printed 'Confirmed by the issuer' about a decision in which no issuer took part -- the reviewer form offered all three methods in a dropdown, and the RPC offered them to any authenticated caller. Hosted production holds three such approvals (two issuer_confirmation, one employer_confirmation, all decider_organisation='CQrityjob'; two sit in live disclosures). They are NOT rewritten, revoked or back-filled: the migration is prospective, its preflight only COUNTS them in a NOTICE, and the application renders that shape through the central trust-presentation helper as 'Review recorded by CQrityjob. Direct source confirmation is not available for this legacy record.' -- documented, never source-verified. The column CHECK on verification_method is untouched, so history stays as written. Placed AFTER the authorisation and already-decided checks and after SP_APPROVAL_REQUIRES_METHOD, so an unauthorised caller learns nothing new and an absent method still reads as absent. Grants restated, not widened; anon still holds nothing; postflight asserts the three new refusals, every pre-existing refusal by name, FOR UPDATE, SECURITY DEFINER, pinned search_path, the one-final-decision index and the append-only trigger. DEPLOY ORDER: safe in either order and safe alone. Applied first, an old bundle's reviewer form can still select a refused method and is told so by name. Applied after the code, the form no longer offers anything this refuses and the employer surface has always sent employer_confirmation. Verified locally: supabase/tests/security_passport_trust_source_containment_test.sql -- all six method/kind combinations, three crafted direct writes, self-verification, employment-only, final-decision uniqueness, and a RE-APPLY of this migration over manufactured legacy rows asserting the holder's record byte-for-byte unchanged; full db-test.sh green. A signed-in holder can therefore POST an invented employment history straight to the Data API, and sp_submit_application_with_cv_source would copy it onto an employer-readable job application.

WHAT THIS MIGRATION DOES. It installs the controlled write path BESIDE the open door rather than instead of it: a server-owned idempotency ledger with no client grants, and cv_create / cv_save / cv_refresh_from_profile / cv_delete -- SECURITY DEFINER, owner from auth.uid(), every factual value derived from the caller's own active sp_experience_periods, sp_claims, sp_passport_profiles, security_career_profiles and profiles rows. Requested fact ids are INTERSECTED with what the caller has, so an unknown or stale id can never add information. Presentation is rebuilt key by key against the bundle, so a citation of a fact the person does not have is dropped. Contact details are validated only where switched on. Every mutation requires the revision the caller was looking at and refuses a stale one with CV_CHANGED; CV_NOT_FOUND is the identical answer for absent and not-yours.

Section 1 RESTATES the existing grants rather than revoking them, so nothing the published application does today stops working the moment this is applied. TRUNCATE was never granted and still is not. Assertions P1-P3 of the test suite pin exactly that.

WHY THE OPEN DOOR IS SAFE MEANWHILE. Because the employer boundary is closed in this same migration. sp_submit_application_with_cv_source now re-checks every carried fact BY VALUE against the holder's live records and refuses with CV_DOCUMENT_STALE_FACTS, so a fabricated CV can still be written but can no longer be sent. It also builds the employer's copy through cv_application_snapshot v2: a contact value whose switch is off has its KEY removed, internal sp_* uuids are replaced by snapshot-local keys, the frozen per-credential verified boolean is dropped, and checked_at is added. Expiry is deliberately not a refusal. Group N of the test suite proves both halves -- that a fabricated employment still lands through the open door, and that the boundary refuses to send it.

Functions are named cv_* and not sp_*: they read cd_report_snapshots for the opt-in Career Discovery insight, and security_passport_phase2_test 5.2 forbids an sp_* body from reading a cd_* object.

DEPLOY ORDER, AS IT HAPPENED. Phase 1 was applied to production on 2026-09-08, on its own, with the published application still writing cv_documents directly and unaffected -- which is what 'additive' was supposed to mean and is now a fact rather than a plan. Next: merge the application PR (#199), which uses only the RPC write path and is correct against BOTH schema states, and publish it. Then, and only then, phase 3 -- 20261103090000_cv_documents_lockdown.sql, PR #202 -- which is the migration that actually revokes the direct grants. It refuses to run unless the four cv_* functions are present, and it must stay a draft until the new application is live.
